entries.value: Foreman.
I was at this port before Don Vittorio.

At eleven, in his office. He and Lorenzo were shouting. Don Vittorio said, ‘We’re finished with that woman, Lorenzo. People have died in America, in France. The Caruso name wasn’t built for this.’ Lorenzo said, ‘You don’t say no to Edda, father.’ Then he said, ‘Come on, let’s talk on the quay,’ and they went out. There’s a camera on the quay; Don Vittorio had it put in.
He turns his cap between his hands.
When did you last see Don Vittorio?

1989. A woman came to the port, a foreigner, Italian with an accent. Don Vittorio called her ‘Dottoressa’. I don’t remember her face; to tell the truth, I never looked at it. She had a man’s watch on her wrist, that I remember; she said it was her husband’s. After that year the Carusos’ ships doubled.
Who is the woman in the photograph in the office?

· In the boot, a half-empty aluminium tin of phosphine tablets and a pair of nitrile gloves; Lorenzo Conte’s fingerprint on the tin.

To shrink the company. The basso, the pizzeria, the funicular, the theatre, the ferry; news every week. ‘Carmela, this isn’t ours, this is that woman’s business,’ he said. He was going to change his will; Lorenzo was to be removed as general manager. He was going to the notary on Tuesday. He died on Monday night.

For forty years Vittorio grew fat on that woman’s money, then he wanted to be a clean old man. Edda doesn’t accept that; nor do I. I hit him on the back of the neck, put him in the container, threw the tablets in, sealed it, hung the plate. In the morning the fumigator would open it; we’d say accident. You won’t find her. Nobody answers that number on my phone; I write, she reads. From Madrid, from Sevilla, I don’t know where.
Everyone at the depot has the seal numbers.
You sealed the container.
At home, in Posillipo. My father-in-law and I had a short business talk in the office; I left at 22.40. He was old; he used to wander the quay at night. He must have gone into a container.
He turns the signet ring on his finger.
Where were you after eleven last night?
We walked on the quay, yes. I closed the container door; it had been left open. I didn’t know he was inside.

CARUSO  /  CHAPTER FINALE
At the port of Napoli, Caruso Marittima’s founder was found dead in a sealed fumigation container.
FILE #052
Crane operator.

The crane cab is forty metres up; I can see the whole quay. Around eleven Don Vittorio and his son-in-law were walking between the containers. Then I saw only the son-in-law; he closed the red container’s door, fixed something to the handles, ran to his car. My shift ends at six in the morning; then I’m off to Salerno, to my new job. I’ll never work here again.
He pushes his hard hat back on his head.
What did you see from the cab in the night?
I’m up there, in the cab.

Don Vittorio decides to change his will and remove his son-in-law as general manager.

On the morning of 13 October 2030, at the port of Napoli, on Caruso Marittima’s Quay 21, the company’s founder Vittorio Caruso (81) was found dead in a container opened after fumigation.

The container was opened by: fumigation technician Samir Haddad. On the quay during the night: foreman Aldo Ruggiero, crane operator Ottavio Mele. The victim’s daughter Carmela Caruso and his son-in-law, the company’s general manager Lorenzo Conte, received the news in the morning.

We do, in a locked cabinet. And the company’s own depot, for grain going onto ships. The general manager and the foreman have the keys to that depot. Last week Mr Lorenzo asked for a tin, said ‘for grain’; I gave it to him against his signature.

It was on the schedule; I was going to put it in at seven in the morning. But when I arrived in the morning there was already a seal on the door, and the fumigation plate was hanging there, saying the gas had been put in. I didn’t put it in. I cut the seal and opened it to air it out. Don Vittorio was inside.

· The first seal on the container door, ‘CM-44817’: from the stack in the Caruso Marittima depot; in the stack’s log, last drawn 12 October 22.51, signed: Lorenzo Conte.
· Fumigation schedule: the container was to be fumigated on 13 October at 07.00; the fumigation firm’s seal is the second seal.
· From the company depot on 6 October, a tin of phosphine tablets, ‘for grain’, signed: Lorenzo Conte. No grain shipment that week.
SEAL AND FUMIGATION RECORDS

The crane operator saw everything from his cab; if he wasn’t asked before the quay footage was opened, he left for Salerno. The foreman gave the last conversation and the photograph, the fumigator the seals, the daughter the will. A justified search found the tablet tin and the number in Spain: 212 messages, not a single reply.
The woman in the photograph has no face; she has a watch. Next city: Sevilla.
Port of Napoli — October 2030

After the deaths stretching from Chicago to Napoli, Vittorio Caruso wanted to shrink the company he had built with the money of the ‘Dottoressa’ who came to the port in 1989, and to remove his son-in-law. Saying ‘you don’t say no to Edda’, Lorenzo Conte took his father-in-law to the quay at night, struck him on the back of the neck, put him in a container, threw in phosphine tablets taken from the depot and closed the door with a fumigation seal.
Who killed Vittorio Caruso?
